sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2017. Change Request Number 2017-017 (submitted by Karsten Legère, Univ. Wien/Gothenburg; supported by Rainer Vossen, Frankfurt): retire [mwx] Mediak; adopted 2018-01-23. Dallas: SIL International. 6 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States (p. 2, sec. 3c-g) that Mediak is a clan name like Mosiro and Kisankasa per Maguire (1948: 7-8), not a glossonym; Rottland & Vossen (1977: 226-230) assign all three clans to Akie; 'there is no Mediak language'. Bibliography p. 5-6: Maguire 1948, Petrollino & Mous 2010, Rottland 1982, Rottland & Vossen 1977.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 3c: 'Mosiro is known among the current Akie community in Tanzania as a clan name, and not as a linguistic variety.. today Mosiro should only be retained as a clan name within the Akie ethnic group.' Confirms the sister code to Mediak was retired on the same grounds; Glottolog keeps Akie under mosi1247.
Nothing on stress. mwx 'Mediak': deprecated, retired 2018-01-23 via CR 2017-017, no replacement code. mwy 'Mosiro': retired 2018-01-23 via CR 2016-029, reason 'Nonexistent', adopted.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page medi1249 'Mediak' (Bookkeeping) and languoid page mosi1247 'Akie' (Nilotic; alt. names Mosiro, Dorobo, Ndorobo; ISO mwy retired), plus Glottolog reference 412954.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. medi1249 is a retired bookkeeping entry with no descriptive references (only the ISO change request). mosi1247 lists two descriptive refs: Heine, König & Legère 2015, The Akie Language of Tanzania: A Sketch of Discourse Grammar (Tokyo: ILCAA, ii+182 pp, grammar sketch) and Heine, König & Legère 2017, A text study of discourse markers in Akie (pp. 147-167); no URL/DOI given for either.
